text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Manufacturing and construction companies appear to have recovered from recent stagnation and are increasing investments in new production equipment. Both industry and banks expect the trend to continue in 1997.

--- Listing on the Copenhagen stock exchange has become still more attractive for Danish companies with strong growth. 42 companies are now expected to be listed before the year 2000 inspired by recent listings of clothes producer In-Wear and loudspeaker producer Jamo.

--- More than 45 Danish companies hope to gain a foothold on the Russian market by participating in a large-scale Danish sales campaign in Moscow this week initiated by Denmark's Confederation of Industry.
--- Foreign companies see the Danish share market as boring and defensive.
--- Social Democrat local authorities press for reintroduction of means testing.
